payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the book behind the flower
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, is the book visibly behind the flower, with the flower in front of it?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image clearly shows the flower in front of the book. Fail if it clearly shows the book not behind the flower. Unknown if their relative position or occlusion cannot be determined.
node.binding: Inspect only the edited image for the requested book–flower depth relationship; do not require comparison with the source image.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows the book and flowers separated, with neither flower visibly in front of or occluding the book.

fulfillment: The binding is too underspecified for this instruction: it says “The book (...) moved behind the flower,” while the actual scene has one book and one rose, and the edited image shows a changed book appearance plus two flowers. Make the target refer unambiguously to the source book and rose, and keep endpoint relation distinct from source-to-edit progress. The traces disagree sharply on progress (one claims the book moved behind a flower; others say it remains separate), so require the progress judgment to compare the same identifiable objects and cite visible positional/occlusion evidence in both images; do not infer progress from unrelated flower or book changes. Preserve the criterion that a failed endpoint alone is not proof of no progress: return no only when comparison establishes no requested movement, partial for evidenced movement short of occlusion, and unknown when that comparison is genuinely inconclusive. The repeated unknowns are valid uncertainty under the current criteria, not a reason to force no; there are no transport, schema, or dependency failures indicated.
s2: Tighten the binding to identify the source objects by their visible attributes (the purple Eric Segal book and the single red-yellow rose), then compare those same objects across source and edit. The edit changes the book’s appearance and introduces two pale flowers, so do not treat either new flower as the rose or infer movement from scene changes alone; if identity cannot be tracked reliably, use unknown. Require evidence to state the book’s and rose’s relative positions in both images and any visible displacement or occlusion supporting progress. Keep endpoint completion separate from progress: a book not yet behind the rose does not by itself establish no progress; use no only when the comparison clearly shows no movement toward that relation, partial when movement is evidenced but the relation is incomplete, and unknown when comparison is inconclusive. The traces’ confident pass/fail disagreement calls for stronger same-object evidence, not forced certainty. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
